text:
Hi,
They're usually formatted in a monospaced font on purpose, not because the actual drafting system in 2016 was a real typewriter. Intelligence and government systems use that specific style to standardize redactions and hide which department or person generated the file. It's a bit of a dead giveaway, but it makes the documents look properly classified to anyone reading them. So the look is mostly a formatting convention, not the actual hardware they used to type it up. I wouldn't bother digging into the actual keyboard, though it does look a bit dated for that year.
Thanks
